SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal pain for the last 2 days; feels hot and sweaty.
- History of presenting complaint:
  - Pain is located in the middle of the lower abdomen.
  - Mild nausea (no vomiting).
  - Reports constipation last week; now resolved, last bowel movement 2 hours ago, normal.
  - Reports slight pink discoloration in urine (suggestive of mild hematuria); first occurrence.
  - No pain on urination.
  - Increased urinary frequency, but reduced fluid intake noted.
  - Increased thirst.
  - No fever (self-recorded temperature ~37°C).
  - No pain higher up in abdomen; no acid reflux.
  - No vaginal discharge.
  - No recent travel abroad.
  - No back pain; no strong smell to urine.
  - Menstrual periods regular; no intermenstrual or postcoital bleeding.
  - Some sweating; no shivering.
- Past medical history: No significant past medical history reported aside from typical mild illnesses (colds, flu).
- Previous surgeries: Internal contraceptive implant in the past (removed about a year ago).
- Medications: None.
- Allergies: Amoxicillin.
- Family history: Mother had breast cancer (treated successfully).
- Social history:
  - Lives with parents.
  - Drinks alcohol (approx. 1 beer, 4 times per week).
  - Does not smoke.

Objective:
- Vitals: Temperature self-recorded once at 37°C (one hour ago).
- No physical examination documented.
- No investigation results documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Lower abdominal pain with urinary symptoms:
   - Assessment: Suspected urinary tract infection.
   - Differential diagnosis: Not documented.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned: 3-day course of antibiotics (specific drug/dose/route/frequency not documented; stated to be taken twice daily for 3 days); instructions to monitor symptoms and seek further care if symptoms worsen, develop fever, back pain, or new symptoms.
   - Relevant referrals: None documented.

Quality checks:
●	Missing clinically expected elements: 
   - No urine dipstick or urinalysis documented.
   - No physical abdominal or pelvic examination documented.
   - Name/dose/route/frequency of antibiotic not specifically documented.
   - No medication reconciliation beyond allergy and current usage.
●	Internal conflicts: None present.
●	Transcript quality: Some minor hesitations, but clinically relevant information is clearly extractable.
